compartment.title: Audited app security posture
compartment.p1:
U: "can you audit the app like a developer auditor and tell me if you see any issues with any of it? Take your time and go through everything"
Comprehensive developer audit of LocalLlmConsole v1.1.5 (.NET 8 WPF, ~320 service files). Found two Criticals: C1 — plaintext API key written to OpenCode config file (`OpenCodeConfigService.Json.cs:53`), bypassing DPAPI protection; C2 — internal exception details leaked in gateway 500 responses (`ModelGatewayService.cs:170`). Also flagged H1 (WSL bash injection surface, later downgraded to Medium after verifying `BashQuote` escaping is correct), H2 (header forwarding via `TryAddWithoutValidation` blocklist), and M3 (HttpClient "leak" — later removed entirely as holding one HttpClient per app lifetime is the correct .NET pattern). Graded: Security B-, Architecture A- (revised from B+), Testing A-.
compartment.p2: Full security audit revealed two genuine Criticals (plaintext API key in shared config, gateway exception leak), several Medium/Low findings, and strong baseline controls (DPAPI, path safety, checksums). One finding was wrong (M3 HttpClient), one over-weighted (H1 WSL injection).
compartment.p3: Audit found C1/C2 criticals, removed M3 (wrong), downgraded H1 (over-weighted), raised architecture grade to A-.
compartment.p4: OpenCodeConfigService; SecretProtector; ModelGatewayService exception leak; BashQuote; TryAddWithoutValidation

facts.CONSTRAINTS: * OpenCode independently reads `opencode.jsonc` for API key — app can't simply write "EMPTY" without breaking the integration. Architectural trade-off requiring IPC redesign, not a quick fix.

compartment.title: Fixed gateway leaks and multi-slot metrics
compartment.p1:
U: "Fix them and while in there investigate why when having more than 1 slot active our metrics are showing wrong numbers (or at least averages look wrong)"
Applied three fixes then bumped to v1.1.6: - **C2 fix** (`ModelGatewayService.cs:170`): Replaced `ex.Message` with generic `"An internal gateway error occurred."` in 500 responses. Full exception still logged via `Trace.TraceError`. - **H2 fix** (`ModelGatewayUpstreamProxy.cs:21-61`): Replaced blocklist header forwarding (forward everything except hop-by-hop + Authorization) with explicit allowlist: `Accept`, `Accept-Encoding`, `User-Agent`, `Cache-Control`. - **Metrics bug** (`RuntimeMetricSummaryTracker.cs:104-108`): llama.cpp returns per-slot gauges labeled `{slot="0"}`, `{slot="1"}`. `First()` grabbed only slot 0's value, so average showed ~10 t/s while live rate correctly showed ~21 t/s with 2 slots. Changed `First` → `Sum` for throughput gauges. Count-based gauges (KV usage, context size) still use `First` — correct for non-additive metrics.
Bumped all version references from 1.1.5 to 1.1.6 across csproj, MainWindow.xaml, MainWindow.State.cs, README.md, and test assertions. Updated release notes. Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Tests: 445/445 passed.
compartment.p2: Gateway exception leak sanitized (generic message), header forwarding switched to allowlist, multi-slot gauge averaging fixed from First → Sum across all active slots. Version bumped to v1.1.6.
compartment.p3: Three fixes shipped in v1.1.6: gateway error sanitization, header allowlist, per-slot gauge summing for correct parallel throughput averages.
compartment.p4: C2 fix; H2 header allowlist; First → Sum gauge fix; v1.1.6 version bump

facts.CONFIG_VALUES: * Gateway request header allowlist: Accept, Accept-Encoding, User-Agent, Cache-Control (Content-Type handled separately). * Throughput gauges use `Sum` across slot labels; non-additive gauges (KV, context) still use `First`.

compartment.title: Added build progress reporting
compartment.p1:
U: "Investigate if there is a way to make the app more responsive during runtime update" → "fix it, add it to the release notes and update the portable version"
Traced full execution path from UI click → `ForegroundTaskApplicationService.RunBusyAsync()` → build workflow → process execution. Found PageHost disabled for multi-hour builds with no intermediate progress (unlike package installs which use `ProgressAsync` callbacks at each step). Added real-time progress: periodic elapsed-time updates every 15 seconds via `RunBuildProgressLoopAsync` in `RuntimeBuildWorkflowService.cs`, dispatched to UI through `Dispatcher.InvokeAsync(() => SetStatus(message))`.
Fixed a bug where fast builds (<15s) would stick on "Building..." for up to 15 extra seconds: progress loop now uses linked `CancellationTokenSource` cancelled immediately after build completes, terminating the in-progress delay instantly.
compartment.p2: Build progress loop polls every 15s with elapsed time display ("Building... (2m 15s elapsed)"). Linked cancellation token ensures fast builds update status immediately without artificial delay.
compartment.p3: Runtime builds now show periodic elapsed-time progress instead of static "Building..." for hours.
compartment.p4: RunBuildProgressLoopAsync; ProgressAsync callback; CancellationTokenSource linked cancel; 15s polling interval

facts.CONFIG_VALUES: * Build progress polling interval: 15 seconds. * Progress format: `"Building... ({elapsed.TotalMinutes:F0}m {elapsed.Seconds}s elapsed)"`

compartment.title: Added checksum-skip confirmation dialog
compartment.p1:
U: "why does it fail to install runtime now?" → log showed `Runtime package asset llama-turboquant-triattention-win-cu13-x64.zip is missing SHA-256 verification metadata.`
Atomic TurboQuant triattention CUDA release doesn't publish SHA-256 checksums. `requireChecksum` was hardcoded `true` at `RuntimePackageInstallFileService.cs:16` — hard rejection with no fallback. Threading a new `RequireChecksum` flag through the full chain (`RuntimePackageInstallRequest` → workflow request → install service). Application service now catches missing-checksum errors, shows confirmation dialog via `ConfirmSkipChecksum` callback wired to MainWindow's dialog service, and retries with `RequireChecksum: false` on "Yes". Dialog text warns: *"Only proceed if you trust the download source."*
compartment.p2: Missing SHA-256 metadata now triggers a user confirmation popup instead of hard-failing. Retry path re-runs install with checksum verification disabled.
compartment.p3: Runtime package installs without published checksums now show skip-verification dialog instead of failing silently.
compartment.p4: RequireChecksum flag; ConfirmSkipChecksum callback; TryInstallOnceAsync retry logic; SHA-256 missing dialog

compartment.title: Fixed gauge metric name substring match
compartment.p1:
U: "why do i see 20 average tokens a second when it's 20+ a slot?" → "in D:\LlamaCppConsole"
The `observedAverageGenerationRate` lookup at line 104 searched for metric names containing `"seconds"`. llama.cpp reports gauges as `llama_tokens_predicted_per_second` — the substring `"seconds"` does NOT appear in `per_second` (ends at `second`, no trailing `s`). Gauge lookup always returned null, falling through to counter-based fallback: `Rate(predictedTokens, predictedSeconds)` where `predictedSeconds` summed per-slot CPU seconds. With 2 parallel slots each running ~120 wall-clock seconds: `9800 / (120.5 + 118.3) = 41 t/s` instead of the correct ~82 t/s wall-clock rate.
Changed `"seconds"` → `"second"` in all three gauge lookup patterns. `"per_second".Contains("second")` is true; counter metrics (`*_seconds_total`) still excluded by `["total"]` filter. Now correctly sums per-slot throughput: `20.1 + 20.3 = 40.4 t/s`.
compartment.p2: Gauge lookup failed because `"seconds"` doesn't match substring in `per_second`. Changed to `"second"`, gauges now resolve and sum correctly across slots.
compartment.p3: Average token rates now display correctly by matching the actual llama.cpp gauge metric name `*_per_second` instead of looking for non-existent `"seconds"` substring.
compartment.p4: "seconds" → "second" substring fix; per_second gauge resolution; ["total"] exclusion filter

facts.CONSTRAINTS: * llama.cpp Prometheus gauges use singular `per_second` (not plural `per_seconds`). Metric name matching must account for this.

compartment.title: Reverted wall-clock average computation
compartment.p1:
U: "How do we fix this so it displays the real average?" → attempted wall-clock cumulative average (`ComputeSessionAverage`) replacing llama.cpp's `_per_second` EMA gauge.
The server log showed actual throughput of `tg = 48.7 t/s` per slot, but UI displayed `27 avg`. Root cause: llama.cpp's EMA blends all slots' per-batch rates — prompt-processing slots feeding zero generation tokens drag the average down. Implemented wall-clock cumulative approach: `(total_tokens_now - total_tokens_at_session_start) / wall_seconds_elapsed`. Prompt-processing slots contribute 0 to numerator, so they don't dilute the average. Then hybridized: use llama.cpp gauge for single-slot (no dilution problem), wall-clock for multi-slot.
U: "looks like my average tokens per second are completely wrong now and keep jumping around all the time, can you reverse it to where it was?" — reverted entirely. Wall-clock baseline had instability with token counter drops during slot resets; hybrid detection (`requests_processing > 1 || processing_slot_counters > 1`) produced erratic switching behavior.
Retained only the `"second"` substring fix (which is correct). Removed: `ComputeSessionAverage` method, `GenerationBaselineCounter`, `GenerationBaselineAt`, `PromptBaselineCounter`, `PromptBaselineAt` state fields, hybrid slot detection logic.
compartment.p2: Attempted wall-clock average to fix prompt-processing dilution of llama.cpp's EMA gauge, then reverted after instability. Kept only the correct `"second"` substring match fix.
compartment.p3: Wall-clock average experiment abandoned due to jumping values during slot resets; reverted to original gauge with corrected metric name matching.
compartment.p4: ComputeSessionAverage (removed); wall-clock baseline (reverted); hybrid slot detection (removed); retained "second" fix

facts.TRAJECTORY_NOTES: * Wall-clock cumulative average (`total_tokens / wall_seconds`) produces unstable readings during slot resets and counter drops. llama.cpp's EMA gauge, while conservative with multi-slot prompt-processing dilution, is more stable for end users.

compartment.title: Fixed LAN mode HttpListener crash
compartment.p1:
U: "Investigate why when i switch to lan mode in the settings the app crashes and when i rerun it it says not access"
Root cause: Windows requires admin privileges to bind `HttpListener` to `http://+:{port}/` (strong wildcard, all interfaces). Enabling LAN mode → gateway restart with `ListenerPrefix = "http://+:{port}/"` → `HttpListener.Start()` throws `HttpListenerException("Access is denied")` → uncaught through `SaveSettingsAsync()` → app crash. On restart, same persisted LAN settings triggered identical crash at `MainWindow.xaml.cs:78`.
Applied four fixes: 1. `ModelGatewayService.cs:46-60`: Caught `HttpListenerException` in `StartAsync()`, wrapped with descriptive message including netsh fix instructions. 2. `ModelGatewayLifecycleApplicationService.cs:62-69`: `RestartAsync()` returns `GatewayStarted: false` + status message instead of throwing. 3. `MainWindow.Gateway.cs:7-17`: Added `StartModelGatewaySafelyAsync()` wrapper with try-catch, logs to `Trace` on failure. 4. `MainWindow.xaml.cs:78`: Startup uses safe wrapper instead of bare restart call.
After fix: LAN mode without admin rights shows status bar error message (no crash), app runs normally otherwise, gateway starts after `netsh http add urlacl` or running as Administrator.
compartment.p2: LAN mode HttpListener access-denied crash fixed with four-layer error handling: catch at source, non-throwing lifecycle wrapper, safe startup method, and user-friendly status messages with netsh instructions.
compartment.p3: Switching to LAN mode no longer crashes the app — graceful degradation with actionable error message instead of uncaught HttpListenerException.
compartment.p4: HttpListener access denied; http://+ binding requires admin; StartModelGatewaySafelyAsync; netsh urlacl fix instructions

facts.CONSTRAINTS: * Windows `HttpListener` binding to `http://+:{port}/` (strong wildcard) requires Administrator privileges. Non-admin users must run `netsh http add urlacl url=http://+:PORT/ user=Everyone` or launch the app as Administrator once.
